content.comment_body: Hello, I am using [product_name] [version_no] in combination with a RADWAG C32 scale and communicating via Modbus TCP. When I increase the number of registers read from the scale, the communication becomes much slower. For example, reading four registers and storing two takes around 4 seconds. What can I do to improve the Modbus TCP communication speed between [product_name] and the RADWAG scale?

Hi, 1. There is a communication interval set for [product_name] (Modbus TCP client). Try disabling this setting and testing again. 2. You can optimize your Modbus data table by reading blocks of registers instead of individual ones. This can help accelerate the communication. 3. Review your network devices. If using routers, ensure that fixed IP addresses are set outside of the DHCP range to avoid conflicts. 4. [product_name] can communicate via Modbus as fast as 80 ms, if the first point is addressed. You should also check if your Radwag device supports this speed. Hope this helps.
Hi, reading a block of registers does improve the communication speed. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report slow Modbus TCP communication between [product_name] [version_no] and a RADWAG C32 scale, especially when reading multiple registers. The bottleneck is due to non-optimized data access and communication settings. Suggestions such as block register reading and network configuration help to significantly increase speed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect efficient and fast Modbus TCP communication between [product_name] [version_no] and their scales, regardless of the number of registers accessed, with minimal delays.
